bottleneck: Chemical DNA synthesis still has per-base error rates and length limits that make large, complex constructs expensive and failure-prone. Assembling megabase-scale synthetic DNA requires hierarchical assembly with verification at every step, and sequence complexity like repeats and high GC content causes dropouts that demand costly resynthesis. Cost per base has fallen but not enough for routine genome-scale writing, and turnaround times stretch to weeks for long fragments.
current_state: Commercial providers routinely synthesize tens of kilobases; megabase projects remain bespoke, multi-year efforts. Enzymatic synthesis promises longer reads but is not yet cost-competitive with phosphoramidite chemistry.
title: DNA synthesis cost and accuracy cap genome writing
why_it_blocks: Reading DNA became cheap; writing it did not. Until synthesis matches sequencing's economics, genome-scale engineering stays a luxury of well-funded consortia rather than a routine tool available to every lab.
